conf.description: Elastic Stack Audit kibana-audit / syslog-raw (pattern-layout audit appender): grok the [%date][%level][%logger] prefix, find %meta's JSON object by brace-depth counting (string/escape aware, not a naive regex), reconstitute _raw into the same NDJSON the json layout produces, then converge onto the json format's own thin-pass-through convention rather than inventing a parallel ECS mapping.

conf.comment: elastic-audit/kibana-audit/syslog-raw. Reconstitutes into the same NDJSON _raw the json-layout produces, then defers exactly like that format's own thin pass-through -- no new ECS mapping invented, per 'do not build a parallel parser... converge onto the json path.' %meta's JSON boundary is found by counting brace depth char-by-char with string/escape awareness, since a naive regex cannot balance nested braces and %message can itself contain stray brackets (the work order's own warning). On any parse failure (missing prefix, unbalanced braces, invalid JSON) the ORIGINAL unparsed line is left in _raw and cribl.audit.parse_error records why -- 'a half-parsed audit line is worse than a flagged gap,' and a dead-letter Route is out of a pipeline's scope. %level/%logger are dropped as documented duplicates of meta's own log.level/log.logger; %date becomes both the reconstituted @timestamp key and Cribl's own _time.

functions.description: document the reconstitute-not-reinvent approach and the parse-failure fallback
split the 3 bracketed prefix tokens from the trailing %meta+%message blob (unanchored, tolerates a leading collector envelope)

brace-depth-counted (string/escape-aware) extraction of the %meta JSON object, reconstitute _raw as the equivalent NDJSON document, set _time from %date, flag any parse failure without touching _raw so the original line survives for investigation
tag the dataset (matching the json format's own tag) and category before Elastic parses the reconstituted _raw, exactly as the json-layout pipeline does
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
